State the leadership question. Identify this as interpretation, not an original measurement. Check first-person claims with the author.

## What the evidence supports

Describe each source's method, setting, result, and limits. Distinguish survey responses, experiments, forecasts, and guidance. State whether a full paper, public summary, or preview was actually read. Do not summarize inaccessible articles.

## My interpretation

Connect the evidence to the question. Explain the reasoning and where reasonable disagreement remains.

## A decision to examine

Give a practical way to inspect a workflow, responsibility, or team design. Label hypothetical examples and calculations.

## What would change this view

Name uncertainties, contrary evidence, and observations that would weaken the argument. Avoid universal staffing predictions.
